page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2d family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs, mapped from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and ships with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2693.38, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21558.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9379.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, registering 1018.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 75.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform within average ranges, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 17164.71 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 26.13 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-16 is its low memory allocation relative to its compute capacity, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive workloads or large in-memory databases. However, its dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide predictable compute performance, making it a cost-efficient option for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include web serving, software compilation, batch processing, and lightweight machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its 135M parameter LLM text generation speed of 242.73 tokens per second.
